text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key, to prove your identity. Be careful with rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, always include error handling in your code, so your application can respond gracefully when something goes wrong, like a failed request or an invalid response.
